sourceEvidence.label: Aviation Dashboard selected R3 implementation evidence

assessment.summary: Kato selected and locally implemented the compatible regional operations contract and central typed runtime-policy contract; the current dirty source and exact traceability contract are machine-bound without claiming a retained candidate, hosted completion, or release.

selection.authorityBoundary: No commit, push, provider contact, Cloudflare mutation, billing, deployment, or publication authority is granted by this selection.

nonNegotiables: Keep Live disabled by default until separately authorized release gates pass.
Do not persist aircraft identity, callsign, registration, coordinates, trails, provider payloads, client IP addresses, or arbitrary error text.
Do not contact a provider, deploy, enable billing, or exercise real aircraft endpoints during local R3 work.
Preserve Replay, Lab, Evidence, unified offline, and v2 behavior.
assumptions: The regional Durable Object topology remains the preferred local baseline.
No measured account-wide rate, billing, hosted availability, or platform-retention evidence was supplied.
Every material non-ignored source change requires a refreshed selected evidence manifest before the local R3 evidence is current.

opportunities.title: Own a privacy-safe operational evidence plane
opportunities.summary: Separate application health from provider health and give operators exact, bounded, privacy-safe state and SLI semantics.
opportunities.diagnosis: Regional coordinators own provider polling truth, but current health and metrics do not expose application faults, valid-empty observations, stale data, partial regional failure, delivery outcomes, or admission outcomes as distinct states.

evidence.claim: The health route aggregates regional objects as one request and does not preserve a partial result when one region rejects.
Hourly, aggregate-only provider poll metrics have a fixed 30-day cleanup boundary.
Provider failures, internal application faults, and successful observations are handled separately internally, but the distinction is not fully retained or projected.
Operational truth has no single owned schema, so a warm object can project an earlier live state without enough reason codes to distinguish stale or valid-empty data.

desiredInvariants: Application availability and provider observation health are separate dimensions.
Valid-empty, stale, disabled, unavailable, rate-limited, and partial-regional states use fixed reason codes.
Every stored or exported operational value remains aggregate-only and bounded.
Health is explicit user action in Evidence and never creates a hidden polling loop.
A dedicated G2 harness cannot retain screenshots, traces, HAR, response bodies, or aircraft detail.

options.title: Extend the existing regional contract
options.summary: Add a versioned operations-health schema, fixed outcome vocabulary, aggregate SLIs, partial-region aggregation, and a comprehensive privacy receipt to existing regional ownership.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The health route must switch to partial regional aggregation and preserve fixed application and provider dimensions.
The existing bounded aggregate schema is extended with application, delivery, admission, outcome, and freshness counters.
The coordinator becomes the owner of stable operational reason codes while retaining no aircraft detail.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fixed enums, recursive privacy checks, and separate no-capture G2 evidence narrow data-leak and health-misclassification paths without adding a new trusted service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Seed privacy canaries across Durable Object, browser, report, test-output, and retained-artifact surfaces and require one aggregate-only receipt.

tradeoffs.assessment: Classification and bounded counters stay inside the existing polling and explicit health paths; no new network hop is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare poll latency, health latency, and event-loop delay before and after at ordinary, 500-aircraft, and 2,000-record fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: A fixed schema adds bounded counters and timestamps but no per-aircraft retention or unbounded queue.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect all stored values and compare heap and Durable Object storage size at retention steady state.

tradeoffs.assessment: Partial aggregation prevents one failed region from erasing the status of healthy regions, while stable reason codes make stale and empty observations deterministic.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault one region, inject internal failures, valid-empty payloads, stale timestamps, rate limits, and recovery, then verify state transitions and backward compatibility.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators receive one application-owned vocabulary and bounded SLI receipt without depending on account logging.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse stale-feed, partial outage, disabled, quota, rollback, and provider-failure runbooks against deterministic fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: The schema can be added alongside the existing response for one compatibility window and rolled back without changing Live delivery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old and new health consumers in parallel, compare projections, then remove compatibility fields only after acceptance.

residualRisks: Application-owned metrics cannot prove Cloudflare account logging, physical deletion, billing, or global availability.
Regional counters do not provide exact cross-region event ordering.

workPackages: Define operations.v1 and pure classifiers.
Add bounded application and provider SLI counters.
Return partial regional health and preserve compatibility.
Add whole-artifact privacy auditing and a no-capture G2 harness.
Project the new dimensions through explicit Evidence health checks.
acceptanceCriteria: All required states and partial failures produce deterministic fixed reason codes.
No canary aircraft or request identity appears in any permitted persistence or artifact surface.
Existing Live, Replay, Lab, Evidence, offline, and v2 gates remain green.
migrationNotes: Keep the existing health fields for one compatibility window.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the new projection and counters while retaining the existing health response and all product routes.

options.title: Create a central OperationsLedger
options.summary: Send bounded regional events to one Durable Object that owns exact cross-region aggregation and retention.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A ledger can own partial aggregation, but the current health route still needs a safe compatibility and failure-isolation change.
Regional coordinators emit fixed bounded events while the ledger owns cross-region projections.

tradeoffs.assessment: One schema and retention boundary narrow semantic drift, but the ledger becomes a new trusted data sink and must reject arbitrary fields.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fuzz event schemas, seed privacy canaries, inspect every retained value, and verify events fail closed on unknown fields.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each regional outcome gains serialization and a cross-object call or buffered delivery path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure regional poll completion and ledger ingestion p95 with one, three, and faulted regions against the current no-ledger baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design adds a retained event or aggregate index and potentially a bounded retry buffer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Set an explicit storage and in-memory queue ceiling, then measure steady state and outage backlog.

tradeoffs.assessment: Exact cross-region ownership improves consistency, but a central object can become an availability and backpressure dependency unless regional delivery fails open.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault, delay, restart, and saturate the ledger, then prove Live polling and delivery continue while bounded evidence gaps are explicit.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators gain exact cross-region correlation and one retention schedule at the cost of another binding, schema, alarm, and incident surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run migration, retention, saturation, replay, and rollback drills with clear alert ownership.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new binding, protocol, storage schema, batching policy, and dual-read compatibility period are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Shadow-write fixed events, compare ledger and regional projections, then rehearse removal without touching the Live feed path.

residualRisks: The ledger may become a regional evidence bottleneck or single logical failure domain.
It still cannot prove platform-level logging and physical retention policy.

workPackages: Design a strict event schema and retention ceiling.
Add a fail-open regional client and bounded retry policy.
Implement the ledger, shadow projection, and dual-read comparison.
Add migration and rollback receipts.
acceptanceCriteria: Ledger failure cannot interrupt provider polling or viewer delivery.
Cross-region projections are exact for accepted events and explicit about dropped events.
migrationNotes: Require a shadow-write and dual-read period before authority moves.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove ledger emission and health reads while regional coordinators retain their existing ownership.

options.title: Use Cloudflare-native analytics
options.summary: Use platform metrics and bounded custom aggregate events as the hosted observability supplement after account-policy approval.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Platform analytics can supplement availability and resource trends, but application-owned exact health semantics and privacy inspection remain necessary.

tradeoffs.assessment: A managed sink reduces custom storage code but expands account policy, role, retention, query, and telemetry trust boundaries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: At G1, inspect account roles, logging, datasets, field policy, retention, export, deletion, and query access before enabling any custom event.

tradeoffs.assessment: Managed writes are likely off the viewer path, but exact Worker overhead is unmeasured for this account and workload.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare poll and request p95 with analytics disabled and enabled using only synthetic aggregate events.

tradeoffs.assessment: Custom in-application historical storage may shrink, but local schemas and bounded current state remain necessary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure Durable Object storage and heap before deciding whether any local aggregate can be removed.

tradeoffs.assessment: Hosted availability metrics add an independent view, while sampling and platform dependency prevent exact event accounting.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare application counters with platform queries across fault injection and confirm gaps are represented, not hidden.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dashboards and account metrics help operations but introduce cloud configuration, budget, role, query, and retention ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document account configuration, alert routes, query receipts, cost ceilings, and disablement before G1 exit.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option requires account approval, bindings or configuration, schema governance, and parallel comparison before reliance.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Treat the platform path as a supplement until synthetic parity and rollback drills pass.

residualRisks: Adaptive sampling prevents exact event accounting.
Platform retention and request metadata are outside local repository proof.
Availability and cost depend on the selected account plan.

workPackages: Approve the account, telemetry, retention, role, and budget policy at G1.
Define an aggregate-only event schema.
Run synthetic parallel comparison and disablement drills.
acceptanceCriteria: No aircraft or request identity field can enter platform custom events.
Cost, sampling, retention, role, and rollback behavior are verified in the authorized account.
migrationNotes: Do not replace application-owned health semantics with sampled analytics.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the analytics binding or emission path and continue with application-owned health.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the existing regional ownership model under current constraints; add a ledger only for a measured exact-correlation need and add platform analytics only after G1 approval.

opportunities.title: Centralize runtime and release policy
opportunities.summary: Make runtime modes, provider egress, origin rules, headers, kill-switch behavior, quotas, artifact privacy, performance budgets, and release receipts derive from one typed contract.
opportunities.diagnosis: Strong controls exist, but their ownership is distributed across Worker construction, routes, provider configuration, Vite configuration, retained artifacts, and workflow tests; generated deployment metadata currently contains absolute local paths.

evidence.claim: Provider origin and regional paths are fixed and fail closed.
Live enablement is read into object state, so a deploy-time change is not itself a demonstrated immediate shutdown mechanism for an existing object.
Candidate retention copies generated text artifacts without a general absolute-path privacy filter.
Generated configPath and userConfigPath values contain the local Windows workspace path.
Development and eventual hosted connection policy need separate release-owned contracts so loopback origins cannot drift into an approved production candidate.

desiredInvariants: Every build and runtime mode has one typed, reviewable, fail-closed policy.
Server-owned disablement stops new admission, provider polling, and established Live sessions without breaking non-Live workspaces.
Retained and published artifacts contain no absolute local paths, usernames, credentials, temporary roots, or unapproved origins.
Static and Worker responses carry target-specific checked security headers.
Admission, provider, delivery, map, bundle, paint, and operating-cost budgets are explicit and mechanically gated.
Runbooks and release receipts use the same stable policy and reason-code vocabulary.

options.title: Patch and document the current controls
options.summary: Sanitize retained artifacts, add checked response headers, remove hosted-target development origins, and document redeploy-based disablement without centralizing ownership.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Canonical allowlisted metadata or an audited sanitizer must remove local path fields before retention.
Target-specific headers and connection policy directly close the known build-policy gap.
A documented controlled redeploy can serve as a slower kill mechanism, but ownership remains distributed.

tradeoffs.assessment: Direct sanitation, header, and origin fixes close known release defects, but future callers and artifacts can still drift across separate controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject sentinel paths and origins, scan every retained byte, and verify headers across root, assets, maps, API, and WebSocket admission.

tradeoffs.assessment: Build-time scanning and response headers add negligible runtime work; no new request hop is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare build duration, artifact size, and static response latency before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: The approach adds bounded build metadata and no persistent runtime component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm runtime heap and Durable Object storage remain within existing variance.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failing builds on privacy or header drift improves release reliability, but redeploy-based disablement is slower and depends on deployment success.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse privacy failure, bad header, bad origin, disable redeploy, failed redeploy, and rollback cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: A runbook and explicit scanners improve operator clarity while duplicated policy still raises review burden.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Have a clean-room operator execute disable, inspect, retain, and rollback procedures using only the runbook.

tradeoffs.assessment: Focused build and documentation changes preserve runtime APIs and can land incrementally.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the complete build, candidate-retention, workflow-policy, and current regression gates after each patch.

residualRisks: Policy can drift between Worker, client, build, test, and runbook owners.
Redeploy-based disablement may not meet a future sub-minute shutdown requirement.

workPackages: Replace or sanitize generated deployment metadata and add an artifact privacy scanner.
Add target-specific checked headers and origins.
Add performance budgets and versioned operator runbooks.
acceptanceCriteria: Sentinel local paths and unapproved origins fail candidate retention.
All response classes carry the approved target-specific headers.
migrationNotes: This can be the first tactical package inside the recommended typed-policy option.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert each focused build control independently; do not retain or release an artifact that fails privacy scanning.

options.title: Create one typed runtime and release policy contract
options.summary: Compile every supported target into one typed policy consumed by Worker, client, build, artifact scanner, tests, receipts, and runbooks.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Artifact allowlists and privacy scanning become required release-policy outputs, while the immediate path fields still need direct removal.
The policy defines object-start, admission, pre-fetch, and established-session disablement semantics.
Build targets derive exact connected origins, headers, mode, and release assertions from one source.
The policy makes isolate admission limits and scope explicit, while account-wide protection still requires G1 platform controls.

tradeoffs.assessment: One fail-closed policy narrows drift across mode, provider, origin, headers, artifact, quota, and shutdown decisions without adding remote authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Generate a target matrix, mutation-test every deny rule, scan retained bytes, and prove every consumer rejects an unknown mode or field.

tradeoffs.assessment: Most decisions compile at build or object start; a small fixed pre-fetch and session policy check should not add a network hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare admission, pre-fetch, publication, and validated-snapshot-to-paint p95 against explicit budgets.

tradeoffs.assessment: A frozen policy object and bounded counters add small constant state with no new queue or per-aircraft retention.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure Worker heap, browser heap, bundle bytes, and Durable Object storage at ordinary and maximum fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Shared reason codes, deterministic shutdown, generated target checks, and rollback receipts reduce inconsistent behavior during disablement and release.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault policy reads, disable during active sessions and polling, exhaust each quota, and verify Replay, Lab, Evidence, offline, and rollback remain available.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runbooks and release receipts can name the same policy epoch, target, reason code, budget, and artifact hashes, reducing operator interpretation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Execute every runbook branch and require machine-readable receipts that cross-check policy identity and retained bytes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing controls must be compiled in parallel, equivalence-tested, and migrated one consumer at a time before old definitions are removed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a dual-policy decision matrix until every current allow and deny result is equivalent, then migrate with per-consumer rollback.

residualRisks: A defect in the central policy can affect several consumers, so schema validation and mutation coverage are release-critical.
Account-wide rate limiting, hosted headers, billing, and platform retention remain G1 evidence.
Sub-minute remote disablement is not provided without a separately authorized control channel.

workPackages: Close artifact privacy and response-header defects first.
Define typed modes, fixed reasons, limits, origins, headers, artifact fields, and policy identity.
Compile policy beside current controls and prove decision equivalence.
Migrate Worker, client, build, scanner, receipts, and runbooks one consumer at a time.
Add shutdown, quota, bundle, paint, maximum-record, incident, and rollback gates.
acceptanceCriteria: No retained or release artifact contains a forbidden path, username, credential, temporary root, or unapproved origin.
Disablement prevents new admission and provider requests, closes established Live sessions, and leaves non-Live workspaces available.
Every supported target passes a generated policy matrix, response-header checks, gzip budgets, 500-aircraft p95 paint, and 2,000-record safety gates.
Release receipts bind policy identity, source identity, artifact hashes, and rollback bytes.
migrationNotes: Land the direct artifact and header fixes before central migration.
Keep current controls authoritative until equivalence evidence passes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the previous consumer one boundary at a time using retained equivalence fixtures; a failed privacy scan remains non-overridable.

options.title: Add a mutable operations control plane
options.summary: Add authenticated, server-owned policy state for sub-minute disablement and global operating controls, built on the typed policy vocabulary.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Mutable server-owned state can immediately change admission, polling, and session behavior, but deterministic local shutdown logic is still required.
A control plane can distribute global operating state, but exact account-wide abuse protection should still use authorized platform controls.
The mutable design still requires direct artifact sanitation and release privacy scanning.

tradeoffs.assessment: Immediate server-owned disablement narrows incident exposure, but an authenticated mutation API becomes a high-authority attack target with replay and privilege risks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model operator identity, least privilege, replay protection, audit privacy, failed authentication, stale policy, lockout, and break-glass behavior before implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runtime decisions gain a policy read, cache, invalidation, or broadcast path on admission and pre-fetch boundaries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cached and cold policy lookup latency, invalidation time, pre-fetch p95, and shutdown propagation against a sub-minute objective.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design adds versioned policy state, caches, operator audit metadata, and possibly bounded propagation queues.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Set and test explicit policy, cache, audit, and queue ceilings under update bursts and outages.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote control improves incident response, while control-plane outage, stale caches, or bad policy can disable healthy service or fail open.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise outage, stale read, conflicting update, bad policy, regional partition, rollback, and fail-closed behavior with active sessions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators gain immediate control but must own identity, authorization, audit, secret rotation, availability, monitoring, and emergency recovery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require named ownership, access review, key rotation, two-person high-risk changes, drills, and evidence retention before G1 exit.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project needs the typed policy first, then identity, state storage, propagation, cache compatibility, audit, staged rollout, and rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Introduce read-only shadow policy, compare decisions, enable mutations for synthetic environments, and promote only after emergency rollback drills.

residualRisks: Operator credential compromise can gain service-wide control.
Control-plane availability and consistency become service dependencies.
Account-wide abuse and billing protection still require platform controls and alerts.

workPackages: Approve the operator identity and authorization model.
Implement the typed policy contract first.
Design versioned mutable state, cache, invalidation, audit, and recovery.
Run synthetic shadow, staged mutation, and emergency rollback drills.
acceptanceCriteria: Only approved operators can make authenticated, replay-resistant, least-privilege changes.
Disablement reaches all regions and active sessions within the approved objective without provider calls after enforcement.
Control-plane failure is deterministic, observable, privacy-safe, and recoverable.
migrationNotes: Do not create a mutation API until an operator identity model and G1 authority are approved.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Freeze mutations, restore the last signed or otherwise integrity-bound policy, and fall back to controlled redeploy-based disablement.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a typed local policy contract and direct tactical release fixes now; defer mutable authority until sub-minute shutdown and operator identity are explicitly approved.

openQuestions: When should the locally verified R3 source be frozen for an independently authorized commit and hosted preflight?
Is controlled redeploy sufficient for the first hosted release, or is sub-minute remote disablement a G1 requirement?
Which Cloudflare plan, account roles, logging policy, retention policy, rate controls, and budget ceiling are authorized for G1 inspection?
Which provider terms and attribution requirements must be satisfied before G2 real-source validation?
